title: The closed-lift indexing category is filtered
statement:
The category $\mathcal N_A(\overline C)$ of [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift]
is filtered.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal N=\mathcal N_A(\overline C)$ with the objects and all compatible algebra maps of the cited definition. The identity $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an open immersion, hence etale by clause (1) of the composition node. The presentation $A=A[\,]/(\,)$ has zero variables and zero relations. Thus $(A,A\to\overline C)$ is an object, even if $A$ or $\overline C$ is the zero ring, so $\mathcal N$ is nonempty. In the literal presentation model take $E=A[\,]/(\,)$ with evaluation isomorphism $e:E\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ and map $E\xrightarrow{e}A\to\overline C$.

source.place: Tag 02GP, lemma-open-immersion-etale; nonemptiness in blueprint proof paragraph 1

proof.text: For objects $(B,q),(B\prime,q\prime)$ set $P=B\otimes_A B\prime$. The affine fibre-product node identifies $\operatorname{Spec}P\to\operatorname{Spec}B\prime$ with the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. It is etale by clause (1) of the base-change node, and its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale by clause (2) of the composition node. If $B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_r)$ and $B\prime=A[y_1,\ldots,y_m]/(G_1,\ldots,G_s)$, the tensor universal property gives $P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_m]/(F_1,\ldots,F_r,G_1,\ldots,G_s)$: maps from each presentation to any algebra are precisely pairs of maps from $B,B\prime$. Hence $P/A$ is finitely presented. The tensor node supplies $p:P\to\overline C$, $p(b\otimes b\prime)=q(b)q\prime(b\prime)$, with $p(b\otimes1)=q(b)$ and $p(1\otimes b\prime)=q\prime(b\prime)$. These inclusions are the required arrows to the common successor. Precisely, let $E$ be the displayed polynomial quotient and $e:E\xrightarrow{\sim}P$ its $A$-algebra isomorphism. Use $(E,p\circ e)$ as the small-model object, with arrows $e^{-1}\circ\iota_B$ and $e^{-1}\circ\iota_{B\prime}$. Their composites with $p\circ e$ are $q$ and $q\prime$, respectively.

Let $f,g:(B,q)\rightrightarrows(B\prime,q\prime)$ be parallel arrows. Put $T_0=B\otimes_A B$ and $\mu:T_0\to B$, $\mu(b_1\otimes b_2)=b_1b_2$. Step 2, applied to the pair $B,B$, shows that $T_0/A$ is etale. Both $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}T_0$ are therefore etale over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, so clause (3) of the composition-cancellation node makes $\operatorname{Spec}\mu$ etale. The tensor node defines $h:T_0\to B\prime$, $h(b_1\otimes b_2)=f(b_1)g(b_2)$. This is the ring map corresponding to the pair $(\operatorname{Spec}f,\operatorname{Spec}g)$ against which the blueprint pulls back the diagonal.

source.place: Tag 02GW, lemma-etale-permanence; blueprint proof paragraph 2, diagonal before pullback

proof.text: Choose the finite generators $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ of $B$ in its presentation and let $J=(f(x_1)-g(x_1),\ldots,f(x_n)-g(x_n))\subseteq B\prime$. Put $Q=B\prime/J$ with quotient $\pi$. The maps $\pi f$ and $\pi g$ agree on $A$ and on the $x_i$, hence on every polynomial in them, so they agree on all of $B$. For any commutative $A$-algebra $D_0$, maps $B\prime\otimes_{T_0}B\to D_0$ correspond by the tensor universal property to maps $u:B\prime\to D_0$ and $v:B\to D_0$ satisfying $u h=v\mu$. Evaluating on $b\otimes1$ and $1\otimes b$ forces $v=uf=ug$; conversely $uf=ug$ implies the required identity on every pure tensor, and thus everywhere. Such $u$ are exactly those killing $J$, and factor uniquely through $Q$. These inverse universal correspondences identify $Q\cong B\prime\otimes_{T_0}B$, compatibly with $\pi$ and $\mu$. In particular $J$ is also the ideal generated by all differences $f(b)-g(b)$, as in the blueprint.

source.place: Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes, tensor universal property in its proof; explicit quotient calculation for blueprint paragraph 2

proof.text: By the affine fibre-product node and step 4, $\operatorname{Spec}Q\to\operatorname{Spec}B\prime$ is the base change of the etale map $\operatorname{Spec}\mu$ along $\operatorname{Spec}h$. Clause (1) of the base-change node and clause (2) of the composition node make $\operatorname{Spec}Q\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale. Write each $f(x_i)-g(x_i)$ as a polynomial $H_i(y_1,\ldots,y_m)$ in the finite presentation of $B\prime$ from step 2. Then $Q=A[y_1,\ldots,y_m]/(G_1,\ldots,G_s,H_1,\ldots,H_n)$, so it is finitely presented over $A$. Since the arrows are compatible, $q\prime f=q=q\prime g$, and $q\prime$ kills $J$. It descends uniquely to $r:Q\to\overline C$, $r\pi=q\prime$. Thus $(Q,r)$ is an object up to its displayed presentation: if $E$ is that polynomial quotient and $e:E\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$ its isomorphism, take $(E,r\circ e)$ and the arrow $a=e^{-1}\circ\pi:B\prime\to E$. Then $(r\circ e)a=q\prime$ and $af=ag$, as required in the literal small model. No injectivity of $q\prime$ and no nonzero-ring hypothesis has been used.

Steps 1, 2 and 5 give respectively an object, a common successor of every pair of objects, and an arrow equalizing every pair of parallel arrows. These are precisely the three conditions defining a filtered category, as recalled in the cited colimit definition (Stacks Tag 002V, definition-directed). The small presentation model retains all compatible algebra maps, so the explicitly conjugated arrows from steps 2 and 5 are morphisms of that model. Therefore $\mathcal N_A(\overline C)$ is filtered.
